Natural_Language: This part provides policies and procedures for using tax clauses in contracts (including foreign contracts), claiming immunity or exemption from taxes, and getting tax refunds. It explains Federal, State, and local taxes on certain supplies and services that executive agencies buy and how these taxes apply to the Federal Government. This information is general guidance for Government personnel and does not cover all tax laws and regulations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_000_a: Part 29 provides policies and procedures for using tax clauses in contracts including foreign contracts; P_29_000_b: Part 29 provides policies and procedures for claiming immunity or exemption from taxes; P_29_000_c: Part 29 provides policies and procedures for getting tax refunds; P_29_000_d: Part 29 explains Federal, State, and local taxes on certain supplies and services purchased by executive agencies; P_29_000_e: This information is general guidance and does not cover all tax laws and regulations
Validation_Notes: Scope statement establishing Part 29 coverage. Five conjunctive elements define the part's purpose. The qualifier that this is general guidance (P_29_000_e) limits the part's authoritative scope. Declarative statement, no conditional logic required.

Natural_Language: Contract tax problems are primarily legal issues and vary widely. Contracting officers must consult the agency's legal counsel when tax issues arise, especially before negotiating with any taxing authority.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_101_a: Contract tax problems are primarily legal issues; P_29_101_b: Tax issues arise in connection with a contract; P_29_101_c: Contracting officer consults agency's legal counsel; P_29_101_d: Consultation occurs before negotiating with any taxing authority
Validation_Notes: Mandatory consultation requirement triggered by tax issues arising. 'Must' creates obligation. The 'especially before negotiating' phrase strengthens the timing requirement for the consultation. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: General provisions governing Federal excise taxes, including tax descriptions and exemption requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_201: General provisions for Federal excise taxes consist of tax descriptions and exemption requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating subsections (a) and (b). Section (a) describes the taxes; section (b) establishes exemption requirements.

Natural_Language: Federal excise taxes are taxes on the sale or use of specific supplies or services. Subtitle D of the Internal Revenue Code, Miscellaneous Excise Taxes 26 U.S.C.4041, et seq., and its regulations (26 CFR parts 40 through 299) cover Federal excise tax requirements. Direct questions in this area to legal counsel. The most common excise taxes are manufacturers' excise taxes and special-fuels excise taxes.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_201_a_1: Federal excise taxes are taxes on the sale or use of specific supplies or services; P_29_201_a_2: Subtitle D of the IRC and 26 CFR parts 40-299 cover Federal excise tax requirements; P_29_201_a_3: Questions about Federal excise taxes shall be directed to legal counsel
Validation_Notes: Definitional and procedural statement. Three conjunctive elements: definition of excise taxes, legal authority citation, and direction to consult legal counsel. The enumeration of common taxes in subsections (1) and (2) elaborates but does not create separate obligations.

Natural_Language: Manufacturers' excise taxes on certain motor-vehicle articles, tires and inner tubes, gasoline, lubricating oils, coal, fishing equipment, firearms, shells, and cartridges sold by manufacturers, producers, or importers.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_201_a_1: Manufacturers' excise taxes apply to specified items sold by manufacturers, producers, or importers
Validation_Notes: Enumerative definition of manufacturers' excise tax scope. Atomic proposition listing covered items. No logical operators needed as this is a single definitional statement.

Natural_Language: Special-fuels excise taxes charged at retail on diesel fuel and special motor fuels.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_201_a_2: Special-fuels excise taxes are charged at retail on diesel fuel and special motor fuels
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement identifying special-fuels excise taxes. Atomic, no operators required.

Natural_Language: Executive agencies must take advantage of available Federal excise tax exemptions. When the law exempts the Federal Government from these taxes, the contracting officer must, unless inappropriate for the circumstances, request offers on a tax-exclusive basis. When no exemption exists, request offers on a tax-inclusive basis.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_201_b_a: Executive agencies take advantage of available Federal excise tax exemptions; P_29_201_b_b: Law exempts Federal Government from excise taxes; P_29_201_b_c: Contracting officer requests offers on tax-exclusive basis; P_29_201_b_d: Circumstances make tax-exclusive request inappropriate; P_29_201_b_e: No Federal excise tax exemption exists; P_29_201_b_f: Contracting officer requests offers on tax-inclusive basis
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex mandatory requirement with two conditional branches. First: 'must' establishes general obligation. Second conditional: when exemption exists AND circumstances are not inappropriate, tax-exclusive basis is required. Third conditional: when no exemption exists, tax-inclusive basis is required. The 'unless inappropriate' creates a negated condition in the antecedent. HIGH-RISK due to multiple material implications.

Natural_Language: Federal manufacturers' or special-fuels excise taxes do not apply in many contracting situations. This includes supplies for the purposes listed in subsections (a) through (f).
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202: Federal excise tax exemptions apply to supplies for purposes in subsections (a) through (f)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Exemptions are disjunctive -- any one of the listed purposes triggers an exemption. A supply need not qualify under all categories, only one.

Natural_Language: The exclusive use of any State or political subdivision, including the District of Columbia (26 U.S.C. 4041 and 4221).
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202_a_1: Supplies are for exclusive use of any State or political subdivision including DC
Validation_Notes: Exemption triggered by exclusive State/political subdivision use. Material implication: if supplies are for exclusive State use, then Federal excise tax does not apply. HIGH-RISK transformation. External legal citation to 26 U.S.C. 4041 and 4221.

Natural_Language: Export shipment to a foreign country or an outlying area of the United States. Shipment must occur within 6 months after title passes to the Government. When claiming this exemption, the words 'for export' must appear on the contract or purchase document. The contracting officer must give the seller proof of export (see 26 CFR 48.4221-3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202_b_a: Supplies are for export shipment to foreign country or outlying area; P_29_202_b_b: Shipment occurs within 6 months after title passes to Government; P_29_202_b_c: Words 'for export' appear on contract or purchase document; P_29_202_b_d: Contracting officer provides seller proof of export per 26 CFR 48.4221-3
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Exemption with four conjunctive conditions: export purpose, 6-month shipment window, 'for export' language on documents, and proof of export to seller. All four must be met for exemption. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Further manufacture, or resale for further manufacture (this exemption does not include tires and inner tubes) (26 CFR 48.4221-2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202_c_a: Supplies are for further manufacture or resale for further manufacture; P_29_202_c_b: Supplies are not tires or inner tubes
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Exemption for further manufacture with explicit exclusion of tires and inner tubes. Two conjunctive conditions required: manufacturing purpose AND not tires/tubes. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Use as fuel supplies, ships or sea stores, or legitimate equipment on vessels of war, including aircraft owned by the United States and guided missiles and pilotless aircraft.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202_d: Exemption for fuel supplies, ships/sea stores, or equipment on vessels of war
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for vessels of war exemption. Subsections (1) and (2) specify included categories (aircraft and guided missiles). Disjunctive relationship -- either category qualifies.

Natural_Language: Aircraft owned by the United States and constituting part of the armed forces.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202_d_1_a: Aircraft is owned by the United States; P_29_202_d_1_b: Aircraft constitutes part of the armed forces
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive conditions for aircraft exemption: US ownership AND armed forces status. Both required. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Guided missiles and pilotless aircraft owned or chartered by the United States. When claiming this exemption, make the purchase on a tax-exclusive basis. The contracting officer must give the seller an exemption certificate for Supplies for Vessels of War (an example appears in 26 CFR 48.4221-4(d)(2)). The IRS will accept one certificate covering all orders under a single contract for up to 12 calendar quarters (26 U.S.C. 4041 and 4221).
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202_d_2_a: Guided missiles or pilotless aircraft owned or chartered by the United States; P_29_202_d_2_b: Purchase made on tax-exclusive basis; P_29_202_d_2_c: Contracting officer provides seller exemption certificate for Supplies for Vessels of War per 26 CFR 48.4221-4(d)(2); P_29_202_d_2_d: IRS accepts one certificate covering all orders under single contract for up to 12 calendar quarters
Validation_Notes: Conditional: when claiming exemption for guided missiles/pilotless aircraft, three procedural requirements must be met. The certificate provision (P_29_202_d_2_d) is informational about IRS acceptance rather than a separate obligation. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: A nonprofit educational organization (26 U.S.C. 4041 and 4221).
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202_e_a: Supplies are for a nonprofit educational organization
Validation_Notes: Simple conditional exemption. If supplies are for nonprofit educational organization, excise tax does not apply. External citation to 26 U.S.C. 4041 and 4221. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Emergency vehicles (26 U.S.C. 4053 and 4064(b)(1)(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_202_f_a: Supplies are emergency vehicles
Validation_Notes: Simple conditional exemption for emergency vehicles. External citation to 26 U.S.C. 4053 and 4064(b)(1)(c). HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Other Federal tax exemptions established by Secretary of the Treasury.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_203: Other Federal tax exemptions consist of communications excise tax exemption and highway vehicle users tax exemption
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for two specific Federal tax exemptions granted by Secretary of the Treasury. Both exemptions exist independently.

Natural_Language: Under 26 U.S.C. 4293, the Secretary of the Treasury has exempted the United States from the communications excise tax imposed in 26 U.S.C. 4251, when the supplies and services are for the exclusive use of the United States. (Secretarial Authorization, June 20, 1947, Internal Revenue Cumulative Bulletin, 1947-1, 205.)
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_203_a_1: Supplies and services are for exclusive use of the United States; P_29_203_a_2: United States is exempt from communications excise tax under 26 U.S.C. 4251
Validation_Notes: Conditional exemption: exclusive US use triggers communications excise tax exemption. Established by Secretarial Authorization. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Under 26 U.S.C. 4483(b), the Secretary of the Treasury has exempted the United States from the federal highway vehicle users tax imposed in 26 U.S.C. 4481. The exemption applies whether the United States owns or leases the vehicle. (Secretarial Authorization, Internal Revenue Cumulative Bulletin, 1956-2, 1369.)
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_203_b_1: United States is exempt from federal highway vehicle users tax under 26 U.S.C. 4481; P_29_203_b_2: Exemption applies whether US owns the vehicle; P_29_203_b_3: Exemption applies whether US leases the vehicle
Validation_Notes: Unconditional exemption for US from highway vehicle users tax. The ownership/lease disjunction clarifies scope but does not limit the exemption. Exemption applies regardless of ownership arrangement.

Natural_Language: Federal excise tax on specific foreign contract payments under 26 U.S.C. 5000C.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204: Section 5000C tax provisions consist of withholding requirements, Form W-14 procedures, exemptions, non-applicability of other exemptions, and additional information
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 5000C tax provisions. All subsections collectively define the framework.

Natural_Language: Title 26 U.S.C. 5000C and its implementing regulations at 26 CFR 1.5000C-1 through 1.5000C-7 require acquiring agencies to collect this excise tax (section 5000C tax) through withholding on applicable contract payments (see 29.402-3, 31.205-41(b)(8)). Agencies merely withhold the tax for the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). All substantive issues regarding the underlying section 5000C tax, such as the imposition of or exemption from the tax, are matters under IRS jurisdiction.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204_a_1: Acquiring agencies are required to collect section 5000C tax through withholding on applicable contract payments; P_29_204_a_2: Agencies withhold the tax for the IRS; P_29_204_a_3: All substantive issues regarding section 5000C tax imposition or exemption are under IRS jurisdiction
Validation_Notes: Mandatory withholding requirement with jurisdictional clarification. Three conjunctive elements: collection obligation, pass-through role, and IRS jurisdiction over substantive tax issues. Cross-references to 29.402-3 and 31.205-41(b)(8).

Natural_Language: According to clause 52.229-12, Tax on Certain Foreign Procurements, contractors subject to the section 5000C tax will complete IRS Form W-14, Certificate of Foreign Contracting Party Receiving Federal Procurement Payments, and submit this form with each voucher or invoice. If a completed IRS Form W-14 is not submitted with a payment request, the default withholding percentage is 2 percent for that payment request.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204_b_a: Contractor is subject to section 5000C tax; P_29_204_b_b: Contractor completes IRS Form W-14; P_29_204_b_c: Contractor submits Form W-14 with each voucher or invoice; P_29_204_b_d: Completed Form W-14 is not submitted with payment request; P_29_204_b_e: Default withholding percentage is 2 percent for that payment request
Validation_Notes: Two conditional requirements: (1) if subject to 5000C tax, must complete and submit W-14 with each voucher/invoice; (2) if W-14 not submitted, default 2% withholding applies. The 'will' operates as mandatory here per regulatory context. HIGH-RISK due to dual material implications. Cross-reference to clause 52.229-12.

Natural_Language: Exemptions from withholding under IRS regulations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204_c: Exemptions from section 5000C withholding consist of regulatory exemptions, offeror-claimed exemptions, and IRS audit provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for three withholding exemption sub-provisions.

Natural_Language: Exemptions from withholding in IRS regulations at 26 CFR 1.5000C-1(d)(1) through (4) are covered in the prescription at 29.402-3(a), which means the contracting officer will not include the provision when one of the 29.402-3(a) exceptions applies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204_c_1_a: Exemption under 26 CFR 1.5000C-1(d)(1) through (4) applies; P_29_204_c_1_b: One of the 29.402-3(a) exceptions applies; P_29_204_c_1_c: Contracting officer does not include the provision
Validation_Notes: When IRS regulatory exemptions align with 29.402-3(a) exceptions, contracting officer omits the provision. Cross-references to 26 CFR 1.5000C-1(d)(1)-(4) and 29.402-3(a). HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: The offeror will claim exemptions under 26 CFR 1.5000C-1(d)(5) through (7) by submitting an IRS Form W-14 with their offer. If not submitted with the offer, exemptions will not apply to the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204_c_2_a: Offeror submits IRS Form W-14 with offer claiming exemptions under 26 CFR 1.5000C-1(d)(5) through (7); P_29_204_c_2_b: Exemptions apply to the contract; P_29_204_c_2_c: Form W-14 is not submitted with the offer
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Dual conditional: submitting W-14 with offer enables exemptions; failing to submit forfeits exemptions. This creates a strict timing requirement. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Any exemption claimed and self-certified on the IRS Form W-14 is subject to IRS audit. Any disputes about imposing and collecting the section 5000C tax are handled by the IRS because this is a tax matter, not a contract issue.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204_c_3_a: Exemption is claimed and self-certified on IRS Form W-14; P_29_204_c_3_b: Exemption is subject to IRS audit; P_29_204_c_3_c: Disputes about section 5000C tax imposition and collection are handled by IRS; P_29_204_c_3_d: Section 5000C tax is a tax matter not a contract issue
Validation_Notes: Establishes IRS jurisdiction over self-certified exemptions and tax disputes. The distinction between tax matter and contract issue is jurisdictionally significant. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: The exemptions in 29.201 through 29.301 do not apply to this section 5000C tax.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204_d_a: Exemptions in sections 29.201 through 29.301; P_29_204_d_b: Section 5000C tax
Validation_Notes: Negative scope statement: exemptions available for other excise taxes do not extend to section 5000C. This prevents misapplication of general exemptions to foreign procurement tax. Cross-references 29.201-29.301. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Additional information about this excise tax on specific foreign contract payments is available at https://www.irs.gov/government-entities/excise-tax-on-specified-federal-foreign-procurement-payments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_204_e: Additional information about section 5000C excise tax is available at IRS website
Validation_Notes: Informational reference to external IRS resource. Atomic proposition, no logical operators needed. Not a requirement or obligation.

Natural_Language: Scope of subpart 29.3 - State and Local Taxes.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_300: Subpart 29.3 covers State and local taxes
Validation_Notes: Scope statement for Subpart 29.3. Atomic proposition. No substantive requirements in the section heading alone.

Natural_Language: Application of State and local taxes to the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_302: Application of State and local taxes to the Government consists of immunity principle and exemption obligation
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. NOTE: Source text contains duplicate section numbering -- two distinct sections are both numbered 29.302. This first instance addresses application to the Government. The second addresses application to contractors/subcontractors. This may be a drafting error in the RFO text. Flagged for human review.

Natural_Language: Generally, purchases and leases made by the Federal Government are immune from State and local taxation. However, whether a specific purchase or lease is immune is a legal question requiring advice from the agency's legal counsel.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_302_a_1: Federal Government purchases and leases are generally immune from State and local taxation; P_29_302_a_2: Whether a specific purchase or lease is immune is a legal question; P_29_302_a_3: Determination of immunity requires advice from agency's legal counsel
Validation_Notes: General immunity statement with qualification. The 'generally' qualifier means immunity is the default but not absolute. When specific immunity is in question, legal counsel must be consulted. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: When economically feasible, executive agencies must take full advantage of all exemptions from State and local taxation. When appropriate, the contracting officer must provide a Standard Form 1094, U.S. Tax Exemption Form (see part 53), or other evidence listed in 29.304(a) to establish that the Government is making the purchase.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_302_b_a: Exemption from State or local taxation is economically feasible; P_29_302_b_b: Executive agency takes full advantage of all exemptions; P_29_302_b_c: It is appropriate to provide evidence of Government purchase; P_29_302_b_d: Contracting officer provides SF 1094 or other evidence per 29.304(a)
Validation_Notes: Two conditional mandates: (1) when economically feasible, must use exemptions; (2) when appropriate, must provide SF 1094 or other evidence. Both use 'must' creating obligations. Cross-references part 53 and 29.304(a). HIGH-RISK due to dual material implications.

Natural_Language: Application of State and local taxes to Government contractors and subcontractors.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_302_con: Application of State and local taxes to Government contractors and subcontractors consists of agency designation, exemption dependence, Government property taxation, and equipment rental taxation
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. NOTE: Second section numbered 29.302 in source text -- duplicate numbering, likely drafting error. This instance addresses contractors/subcontractors.

Natural_Language: The Government does not normally designate prime contractors and subcontractors as agents of the Government for claiming immunity from State or local sales or use taxes. Before any activity claims that a contractor is a Government agent, refer the matter to the agency head for review. Include all relevant data and a thorough analysis of all relevant legal precedents with the referral.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_302_con_a_1: Government does not normally designate contractors as agents for State/local tax immunity; P_29_302_con_a_2: Activity claims contractor is Government agent for tax purposes; P_29_302_con_a_3: Matter is referred to agency head for review; P_29_302_con_a_4: Referral includes all relevant data and thorough analysis of legal precedents
Validation_Notes: Default rule with conditional exception process. If agent claim is made, mandatory referral to agency head with supporting documentation. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: When purchases are made by a prime contractor or subcontractor rather than directly by the Government, the right to exemption from sales or use tax may not depend on the Government's immunity from direct taxation by States and localities. Instead, it may depend on provisions of the specific State or local law, or in some cases, the transaction may not be expressly exempt from the tax. Protect the Government's interest by following the procedures in 29.101.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_302_con_b_1: Purchases made by contractor rather than directly by Government; P_29_302_con_b_2: Exemption right may depend on specific State or local law provisions; P_29_302_con_b_3: Transaction may not be expressly exempt; P_29_302_con_b_4: Government interest protected by following procedures in 29.101
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: When contractor purchases, exemption analysis shifts to state/local law. Mandatory to follow 29.101. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Often, property owned by the Government (including property acquired under progress payments or the Government property clause) is in a contractor's or subcontractor's possession. States or localities may claim the right to tax Government property directly or to tax the contractor's or subcontractor's possession of, interest in, or use of that property. In such cases, the contracting officer must seek review and advice from the agency's legal counsel on the appropriate action.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_302_con_c_1: Government-owned property is in contractor or subcontractor possession; P_29_302_con_c_2: State or locality claims right to tax Government property or contractor's possession/interest/use; P_29_302_con_c_3: Contracting officer seeks review and advice from agency's legal counsel
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandate: Government property in contractor possession AND state/local tax claim triggers mandatory legal counsel consultation. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: Indefinite-delivery contracts for equipment rental may require the contractor to provide equipment in any state. States and local governments impose various taxes on equipment leased to the Government, and the tax amounts can vary significantly among jurisdictions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_302_con_d_1: IDCs for equipment rental may require equipment provision in any state; P_29_302_con_d_2: States and local governments impose various taxes on equipment leased to Government; P_29_302_con_d_3: Tax amounts vary significantly among jurisdictions
Validation_Notes: Informational statement about tax variation risk. No mandatory requirement. Three conjunctive factual observations.

Natural_Language: North Carolina Sales and Use Tax Act provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_303: NC Sales and Use Tax Act provisions consist of refund authority, filing requirements, and annual process
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for NC Sales and Use Tax Act. Three subsections define the refund and compliance framework.

Natural_Language: The North Carolina Sales and Use Tax Act allows counties and incorporated cities and towns to receive an annual refund from the Secretary of Revenue for sales and use taxes indirectly paid on building materials, supplies, fixtures, and equipment that become part of or are attached to any building or structure built, altered, or repaired for these counties and incorporated cities and towns in North Carolina. In United States v. Clayton, 250 F. Supp. 827 (1965), the court ruled that the United States is entitled to the refund but must follow the Act's refund procedure and regulations to recover what it is due.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_303_a_1: NC Sales and Use Tax Act allows annual refund for indirectly paid taxes on building materials, supplies, fixtures, equipment; P_29_303_a_2: US is entitled to the refund per US v. Clayton 250 F. Supp. 827 (1965); P_29_303_a_3: US must follow the Act's refund procedure and regulations
Validation_Notes: Refund entitlement with procedural compliance requirement. Court ruling creates legal precedent requiring adherence to established procedures. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Natural_Language: To receive the refund, the Act requires claimants to file a written request within 6 months after the end of their fiscal year, supported by records, receipts, and information that the Secretary of Revenue requires. Claimants will not receive a refund for applications filed late or not meeting the Secretary of Revenue's requirements. These requirements include certified statements from contractors showing cost of property purchased per vendor and taxes paid.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_303_b_a: Claimant files written request within 6 months after fiscal year end; P_29_303_b_b: Request supported by required records, receipts, and information; P_29_303_b_c: Refund is received; P_29_303_b_d: Application filed late or does not meet requirements; P_29_303_b_e: Government obtains certified statements from contractor per vendor
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex filing requirement with positive and negative conditions. Timely/proper filing yields refund; late/deficient filing forfeits. Certified statement is mandatory. HIGH-RISK due to multiple material implications.

Natural_Language: The clause prescribed at 29.401-2 requires contractors to submit certified statements disclosing North Carolina State and local sales and use taxes paid during the 12-month period ending the previous September 30 to contracting officers by November 30 each year. The contracting officer must ensure contractors comply with this requirement and obtain the annual refund to which the Government is entitled. The refund application must be filed annually before March 31.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_303_c_a: Contractors submit certified tax statements (period ending Sept 30) to COs by Nov 30 annually; P_29_303_c_b: CO ensures contractor compliance; P_29_303_c_c: CO obtains annual refund; P_29_303_c_d: Refund application filed annually before March 31
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive mandates with specific deadlines: contractor Nov 30, CO compliance oversight, CO refund recovery, application Mar 31. Cross-reference to 29.401-2.

Natural_Language: State and local tax exemptions provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_29_304: State and local tax exemption provisions consist of general guidance, evidence requirements, and proof procedures
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for three subsections covering exemption procedures.

Validation_Notes: Permissive authority with conditional guidance. Either doubt or court challenge triggers appropriateness of special treatment. HIGH-RISK due to material implication.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Four sub-provisions for different contract-type scenarios. All governed by reasonable basis threshold.

Natural_Language: Service, as used in this section, is defined in the Gross Receipts and Compensating Tax Act of the State of New Mexico, Sec 7-9-3(S) NMSA 1978, and means all activities engaged in for other persons for a consideration, which activities involve predominantly the performance of a service as distinguished from selling or leasing property.
